q: What was the first satellite launched into space?
explain: Sputnik 1 was launched by the Soviet Union on October 4th, 1957, becoming the first satellite launched into space.

options: It carried the first human into space
It contained a dog named Laika
It was the first weather satellite
It was launched by the United States
explain: Sputnik 2 was launched almost a month after Sputnik 1 and contained a dog named Laika.

q: What satellite did the United States launch in response to Sputnik, and when?
explain: In response to the Soviet launches, the United States launched Explorer 1 on January 31st, 1958.
Trios was launched in 1960 and was the first weather monitoring satellite.

q: What made Telstar, launched in 1962, significant?
options: It was the first active communications satellite, allowing live television across the Atlantic
It was the first satellite to orbit the moon
It was the first geostationary satellite
It carried the first GPS receiver
explain: Telstar was launched in 1962 and was the first active communications satellite, allowing live television to be transmitted across the Atlantic Ocean.

q: What was Early Bird, launched in 1965?
options: The first satellite to reach medium Earth orbit
The first geostationary satellite for communication purposes
explain: Early Bird was launched in 1965 and served as the first geostationary satellite for communication purposes, allowing international phone calls and television broadcasts.

q: When were Landsat imaging satellites first launched, and what makes the program notable?
options: 1972; it is the longest running continuous satellite-based Earth observation program
1978; it was the first GPS program
1990; it captures imagery of the universe
1965; it was the first communication satellite program
explain: Landsat imaging satellites were first launched in 1972 and is now the longest running continuous satellite-based Earth observation program.

q: When was the first global positioning satellite launched?
explain: Global positioning satellites were initiated and the first was launched in 1978.

q: What was the purpose of the Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990?
options: To capture imagery of the universe
explain: The Hubble Space Telescope was launched in 1990 to capture imagery of the universe.

q: What development made satellite imagery available to the public on a large scale in the 1990s-2000s?
explain: Google Earth made satellite imagery available on a public scale during this era, alongside GPS becoming available to consumers.

q: Which two satellite systems require a paid subscription for near real-time monitoring at sub-meter resolution?
explain: SkySat (0.57-to-1.0-meter resolution) and Pleiades Neo (0.3-to-1.2-meter resolution) both offer near real-time monitoring at the cost of a paid subscription.
